title: Early Intervention for ME: Regional & State Contacts
before:
The Early Intervention for ME sites serve the various geographical regions of Maine.

Download the town lookup directory to find which region is closest to your town. 
 

Use the search bar to find the closest office in your county. 

Region / Reach Address Phone Number
Cumberland County and select towns in Sagadahoc & Androscoggin counties 1011 Forest Avenue, Portland, ME 04103 207-781-8881
Aroostook County and select towns in Washington & Penobscot counties 985 Skyway Street, Presque Isle, ME 04769 207-746-4490
Hancock & Washington counties 116 O'Brien Avenue, Sennett Hall, Machias, ME 04654 207-255-4892
Select towns in Androscoggin, Kennebec, Lincoln, & Sagadahoc counties 5 Gendron Drive, Suite 1, Lewiston, ME 04240 207-795-4022
Knox & Lincoln counties and select towns in Sagadahoc & Kennebec counties 91 Camden Street, Suite 108, Rockland, ME 04841 207-594-5933
Oxford County and select towns in Androscoggin, Cumberland, & Franklin counties 16 Madison Avenue, Oxford, ME 04270 207-743-9701
Oxford County and select towns in Androscoggin, Cumberland, & Franklin counties 60 Lowell Street, Rumford, ME 04276 207-369-0132
Select towns in Kennebec, Somerset, Franklin, Androscoggin, & Waldo counties 325 E. Kennedy Memorial Drive, Waterville, ME 04901 207-877-2498
Penobscot, Piscataquis, Hancock, & Somerset counties and select towns in Waldo & Aroostook counties. 250 State Street, Brewer, ME 04901 207-947-8493

York County and select towns in Oxford & Cumberland counties.

 39 Limerick Street, Arundel, ME 04046 207-985-7861

 

Contact

If you have questions about Early Intervention for ME, please contact a member of the Maine Department of Education Early Intervention team at one of our regional sites, or through our referral line at 877-770-8883.

decisions.label: Let a column of short entries keep them on one line
decisions.why: 1 column holds nothing longer than sixteen characters and sits in a table that also has a column of paragraphs. The layout sizes a column by its longest unbreakable run, so "Step 1" asks only for the width of "Step" and the paragraph column takes the rest — which is how "Step" and "1" end up on separate lines in a column with room to spare beside it. Held on one line, the column asks for what it needs. Nothing is widened by force and no word changes.
